intro: Pick the sentence that best explains why the evidence matters.

items.stem: Evidence: Abigail Adams asked John to “remember the ladies.” Which sentence best explains why it matters?

options.1: Abigail Adams wrote a letter to John Adams in March 1776.
options.2: This shows the fight for liberty in 1776 left women out, and some women knew it.
options.3: John Adams later became the second president.
options.4: Letters were the main way people communicated in 1776.

hints: Which choice says what the evidence shows, not just what it is?
items.reason: It goes past what the letter says to why it matters: liberty in 1776 wasn't meant for everyone.

items.stem: Evidence: Under Article VIII of the Articles, the states collected the taxes for the national treasury. Which sentence best explains why it matters?

options.1: Article VIII of the Articles is about taxes.
options.3: This shows Congress had to ask the states for money and couldn't make them pay, so the national government stayed broke.

items.reason: It connects the rule to its effect: a Congress that depends on the states for money stays broke.

items.stem: Evidence: In Marbury v. Madison, Marshall said the Constitution wins when a law conflicts with it. Which sentence best explains why it matters?

options.1: This shows the Supreme Court claimed the power to strike down laws, a check on Congress courts still use today.
options.2: Marbury v. Madison was decided in 1803.

hints: Three choices are facts. Which one explains?
Look for what the Court gained.
items.reason: It says what the ruling did and why it still matters. The other three are facts with no “so what.”
